steps.title: The black rooster
steps.body: Chianti Classico DOCG covers the original zone between Florence and Siena, with villages like Greve, Radda, Gaiole and Castellina. Its symbol is the black rooster, gallo nero. It must be at least 80% Sangiovese, with native or international grapes for the rest; white grapes were banned in 2006.

steps.title: Three levels
steps.body: Chianti Classico has three levels: Annata, at least 12 months' ageing; Riserva, 24 months; and Gran Selezione, introduced in 2014, from estate grapes, at least 30 months and, since 2021, at least 90% Sangiovese. Since 2021, labels can name 11 UGAs, Unità Geografiche Aggiuntive, villages like Panzano and Radda.

steps.prompt: Order these Chianti wines by minimum ageing, shortest first.
steps.explanation: Plain Chianti is a separate, broader DOCG with lower requirements; Gran Selezione is the top.

steps.title: Chianti versus Classico
steps.body: Chianti DOCG is a separate, much larger area surrounding Chianti Classico, with seven sub-zones like Chianti Rufina and Colli Senesi. Rules are looser: at least 70% Sangiovese. Quality varies, from simple to excellent; Rufina, in the cool hills east of Florence, is often the best.

steps.prompt: What is the symbol of Chianti Classico?

steps.title: What you learned
points: Chianti Classico is the historic heart, at least 80% Sangiovese
Annata, Riserva and Gran Selezione are its levels
Chianti DOCG is broader, with seven sub-zones
